name: Rose Castor
lede: Rose Castor is a dusty, reddish gray recorded by Maerz and Paul in 1930.

sections.title: A late, dusty rose-gray
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary gives Rose Castor a first recorded date of 1926, at plate 54 C 2 [1]. The name pairs rose with castor, though our sources do not explain whether castor here points to the beaver-fur color sense of the word or to a dye, so that link is undocumented here [1]. The ISCC-NBS system does not carry a separate block for this exact name in our data [2].

The nearest named color is [[dusty-rose-brown|Dusty Rose Brown]], 3.2 units away; the library itself lists this as the closest recorded entry [2]. [[zircon-grey|Zircon Grey]] sits an equally close 3.2 units off, and [[crocus-martis|Crocus Martis]] is 3.4 units away [2]. In LCH terms Rose Castor measures lightness 51, chroma 8, hue 20 degrees[2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds Rose Castor in 186 of 23,781 paintings, 0.78 percent, as photographed, more common than 57 percent of the archive's named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 30 of 1,674 paintings, at 3.3 times the expected rate, and is most over-represented in French paintings, at 2.3 times the expected rate [3]. It most often turns up as a light tone, in 29 percent of its paintings [3]. The earliest match is dated 1452, in a work by Bartolomeo Caporali, 478 years before Maerz and Paul's 1930 record of the name — a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof of a dye or pigment, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. [[fontainebleau|Fontainebleau]], a separate library name, sits a little further out, at 4.9 units, from Rose Castor [2].
